question: In a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas, what is the required staff-to-participant ratio for participants in kindergarten and above? Give the number of participants per staff member.
quote: The following staff to participant ratios shall be maintained: ... Kindergarten and above ... Number of Staff ... 1 ... Number of Children ... 18
notes: Kindergarten and above is the only age band in the OST rulebook. Tighter ratios apply to swimming (1:8, 1202.2), risky field trips (1:9, 404.1.d) and the sick care component (1:5, 1800 301.1).

question: In a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas, what is the minimum age for staff members, apart from the limited exception for some younger workers?
quote: Staff members in an Out-of-School Time (OST) Facility shall be age eighteen (18) years or older
notes: Exception: 16- and 17-year-olds may work if they have no disciplinary control, are never left alone with participants, are under direct supervision of an adult staff member at all times, and are high school graduates/GED holders or enrolled in high school or a GED curriculum.

question: Under Arkansas's minimum licensing requirements, a director of a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas who has no college degree may qualify through experience. How many years of experience in early childhood or elementary education are required on that path (along with earning a credential within two years of employment)?
quote: Eight (8) years of experience in Early Childhood or Elementary Education and completion of one (1) of the following, within two (2) years of employment
notes: The credential may be an Out of School Time Credential, CDA, Director's Credential or equivalent, or a Technical Certificate in ECE. Other paths: bachelor's degree in ECE, elementary education, child/youth development or a related field; bachelor's in another field plus 4 years experience, a CDA/OST credential, or 9 college hours in child/youth development; or an associate degree in a related field plus 6 years experience. Directors must also be 21 or older.

question: In a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas, how many hours of approved training must each staff member who works directly with participants complete each year?
quote: All staff members who work directly with participants shall obtain at least fifteen (15) hours of training ... each year
notes: Directors and assistant directors/site supervisors also need 15 clock hours a year (303.6). 307.4.b likewise requires 15 hours of job-specific training each calendar year. Training must be registered with the DCCECE Professional Development Registry or approved by the Department of Education or Higher Education.

question: In a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas, what is the minimum usable indoor floor space required per participant?
quote: Twenty-five (25) square feet per participant of usable floor space shall be required for indoor activities
notes: Bathrooms, kitchen and hallways are excluded. Covered pavilions used by programs whose major component is outdoors must also provide 25 square feet per participant (801.6).

question: In a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas, how much outdoor play area is required per child on the playground at one time?
quote: provide at least seventy-five (75) square feet per child present on the playground at any time
notes: Measured per child present on the playground at any time, not per licensed capacity. The area must be fenced or otherwise enclosed.

question: In a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas, what must staff have from the parent before giving medication to a participant?
answer: Signed parental permission that includes the date, drug name and type, time, dosage, length of time to give it, and the reason
quote: Medication shall be given to participants only with signed parental permission which includes date, type, drug name, time, and dosage, length of time to give medication, and what the medication is being given for
notes: Medication must be in the original container with a child-resistant cap, not expired, and labeled with the participant's name. Prescription medication only as directed by the participant's physician (1101.7).

question: How often must fire drills be practiced in a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas?
quote: Fire and tornado drills shall be practiced as follows: a. Monthly
notes: Fire and tornado drills must be on separate days and at different times of day, and conducted during all hours participants are in care (1201.7.b, e).

question: In a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas, how long must staff, participant and facility records be maintained, unless a rule says otherwise?
quote: The records shall be maintained for three (3) years unless otherwise indicated
notes: Licensing compliance forms (DCC-521) must also be available for 3 years (601.2); transportation rosters are kept 1 year (602.1.b).

question: In a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas, how soon must an injury that requires the attention of medical personnel be reported to the Licensing Unit?
quote: Injuries that require the attention of medical personnel shall be reported to the parent immediately and to the Licensing Unit within one (1) business day
notes: Deadline is for the licensing agency (Licensing Unit). Parents must be told immediately, and parents must be notified of all injuries.

question: In a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas, besides the director and the assistant director or site supervisor, what percentage of the staff on site at any given time must hold first aid and CPR certification?
quote: The director, assistant director or site supervisor, and fifty percent (50%) of the facility staff that are on site at any given time shall have a certificate of successful completion of first aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR)
notes: Training must follow American Heart Association or American Red Cross guidelines and include hands-on skills testing; online-only certification is not accepted. On vehicles, at least one adult must be CPR and first aid certified (1301.3.d).

question: In a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas, how far apart must cots, mats and other sleeping equipment be kept?
quote: All sleeping equipment shall be kept at least one foot (1') apart
notes: OST rulebook has no cribs; this applies to cots and mats used at rest time.

question: Under Arkansas's minimum licensing requirements for out-of-school-time facilities, what is the maximum length of a New Provisional license issued to a newly opened facility?
quote: A New Provisional license shall not exceed twelve (12) months in length
notes: This is the provisional license term. The rulebook states no fixed term for a Regular license; facilities pay an annual license fee while in compliance (104.1).

question: In a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas whose building was licensed on or after November 1, 2002, what is the maximum group size for participants in kindergarten and above?
quote: Kindergarten and above ... 18 ... Group size shall be limited to two (2) times the number of children allowed with one (1) staff member
notes: Group size is twice the one-staff ratio (2 x 18 = 36). It does not apply to periodic or special group activities, meals, rest times, transitions, outdoor time, field trips or special occasions (302.1). Structures licensed before November 1, 2002 are exempt.

question: On a field trip from a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas that involves a risky activity such as rock climbing, horseback riding or canoeing, to what staff-to-participant ratio must supervision be adjusted? Give the number of participants per staff member.
quote: Ratios shall be adjusted to a 1:9 depending on the risk associated with the field trip activity or to maintain proper supervision of all participants in attendance on the field trip
notes: Normal ratio is 1:18; the rule tightens it to 1:9 based on the risk of the activity or to keep proper supervision.

question: When participants from a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas use a swimming pool for water play (not an authorized swimming instruction program), what staff-to-participant ratio applies? Give the number of participants per staff member.
quote: Adult supervision of the children shall be provided at all times, with grouping based on a 1:8 staff to participant ratio
notes: Does not apply during an authorized swimming instruction program. One person with current lifesaving certification must be present at all times; lifeguards may count in ratio only under 1202.3 conditions.

question: In the sick care component of a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas, what staff-to-participant ratio must be maintained? Give the number of participants per staff member.
quote: Out-of-School Time (OST) Participant 1:5, Maximum group size ten (10)
notes: Maximum group size in sick care is 10.

question: In a licensed out-of-school-time (OST) facility for school-age children in Arkansas, when a participant in second grade or above is allowed a short-term activity out of staff sight and hearing (such as going to the restroom), how often must staff contact the participant?
quote: Staff shall contact the participant at least every ten (10) minutes
notes: Only for participants second grade and above who can handle the responsibility; they must be accompanied by at least one other participant and a monitoring system (e.g. two-way radios) must be in place. If the participant will be gone longer than 10 minutes, staff should first contact the responsible adult who will supervise.
